summary: The bench never measures RLS: it runs as the compose superuser, and its policy breaks for a real app role
detail: compose.yml makes delta the bootstrap superuser, so every adapter in bench/run.ts (and the published results-0.3.0.md) ran with the policy bypassed. Run as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role, the bench policy throws 22P02: after a transaction-local set_config commits, a pooled connection reads app.user_id as '' not NULL, and ''::int fails; rls.md prescribes NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::int. Fix: (1) NULLIF in bench/schema.ts; (2) run the adapters as an app role (two pools as rls.md: admin for applyFramework, schema and seed; app role with USAGE/DML and EXECUTE for writeOp), by BENCH_APP_PG_URL or SET ROLE; (3) refuse to run when rolsuper or rolbypassrls; (4) correct bench/README.md and relabel or re-run results-0.3.0.md. Measured (PG 16, loopback): RLS adds ~5 us to a static UPDATE but ~490 us (~20%) to a delta_apply_as write, the generic engine re-planning the policy in its dynamic queries. Acceptance: bun run bench passes as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role, refuses a superuser or BYPASSRLS role, and the README and results say what is measured. Note 2026-10-15: Postgres is moving to dzql (compiled); this bench, and the 20% it found, go with it.

summary: An undo or redo walked every chain its cursor ever began to find its entry: it slowed as the cursor's ledger grew
detail: nextUndo/nextRedo ran a recursive CTE over every chain the cursor began (1 ms at 3,000 entries of one cursor, 3.3 ms at 10,000). Ported dzql's fix (blueshed/dzql#35, _delta_ledger_tip): newest first among the cursor's own entries on its (cursor, id) index, skip an entry something walked, depth up undoes to the chain's write (this cursor's, undoable), back an even depth, forward an odd one undoable, a redo stops at the cursor's last write. Proved equal to the old query over seeded runs through the API; a long history's lookup takes ~30-40 SQLite VM steps where the old took ~120,000 (sqlite3_stmt_status via bun:ffi).
